newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fire at German factory releases poison gas.
newsitem.headline: Fire at German factory releases poison gas.

text.p: A huge fire at a chemical factory caused poisonous gas to pour into the centre of the Bavarian town of Memmingen on Thursday but nobody was injured, police said.
According to initial readings the cloud of gas contained traces of cyanide and ammonia, but police said the fire was now under control and there was no longer any health danger.
The fire started at 3 a.m. (0200 GMT) in a factory hall where cleaning fluids were produced, and spread to another building.
Four apartment buildings near the factory were evacuated. Warnings broadcast on the radio and over loudspeakers told the town's 40,000 citizens to keep doors and windows tightly shut.
The police said they had detained a probable arson suspect, but gave no further details of the man or his possible motives for starting the fire.
